blocks.content: The Advocate General is the highest law officer in the state.

rows: Qualified to be a Supreme Court Judge
Qualified to be a High Court Judge

items: The term of office of the Advocate General is NOT fixed by the Constitution, nor does the Constitution contain specific grounds for removal.
Under Article 177, the Advocate General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the State Legislature, but does NOT have the right to vote.
The Advocate General receives remuneration as determined by the Governor, not drawn from the Consolidated Fund of the State directly as a fixed constitutional salary.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 165 of the Constitution of India provides for the constitutional office of the Advocate General for the State.
The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor and holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
To be eligible, a person must be a citizen of India and qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court.
The remuneration of the Advocate General is determined by the Governor, as it is not fixed by the Constitution.
The Advocate General enjoys all the privileges and immunities that are available to a member of the State Legislature.
